name: Kinetic type stagger
one_line: Words or glyphs enter one after another on offset onsets, so a line builds rather than appears
summary: Text arrives in pieces, each starting a little after the last, so the eye is steered along the line in reading order. It gives a title rhythm and emphasis and suits short statements. Uneven offsets read as sloppy, and an over-long cascade makes the viewer wait for the message to finish building.

routes.one_line: Per-word or per-glyph elements animated with the Web Animations API, seeked per frame

steps.does: Give each word or glyph its own animation, onset offset by index

limits: The tool's fixture staggers dots, not text; splitting text into elements is not exercised
Evidence covers opacity and transform; blur, clip and variable-font axes are untested

routes.one_line: Per-word or per-glyph elements staggered on an Anime.js timeline, seeked per frame

steps.does: Stagger the entrances of the split text elements along one timeline

limits: The tool's fixture staggers dots, not text; splitting text into elements is not exercised
Springs are outside the evidence scope, so overshoot must be built from eased tweens

routes.one_line: Glyph or word meshes in a Three.js scene, each entering on its own offset

steps.does: Typeset the text as SDF meshes the scene can address per glyph
Render the scene with each mesh's entrance driven from t

limits: Text evidence is one local font under software GPU; complex scripts and other fonts are untested
No fixture staggers glyphs; per-glyph addressing is unproven here

source: references/typography §9c, references/motion-director §4.1; tool records as of 2026-11-20
